thread:
zoe: Quick post-all-hands thread for security/compliance items that came up. I'll collect questions and assign owners.

matt: Thanks Zoe. First Q: SOC2 status and whether Type II will cover Private deployments.

aya: SOC2 update: Type I is done (May). Type II audit window targeting Apr-May with report expected by late Q3. Type II scope will include hosted API and Dedicated; Private (customer-managed infrastructure) will be documented but typically outside our auditee boundary unless customer requests Redwood-hosted control plane in scope. We'll publish a scope matrix.

darius: For Private customers: can they require Redwood to rotate CMKs on their behalf or must rotation be performed client-side?

aya: BYOK model: we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) with envelope encryption. Customers can perform rotation in their KMS; Redwood supports key aliasing so a rotated key can be picked up without downtime. If a customer wants Redwood to perform rotation, we need a contractual SLA and key-access workflow (rare).

sanjay: Which KMSes do we integrate with today? Any roadmap for Hardware Security Modules (HSM) / CloudHSM?

eli: Current integrations: AWS KMS (multi-region), GCP KMS. Azure Key Vault is in early testing. For HSM-level integration, we have a pilot for CloudHSM/PKCS#11 for one enterprise customer; general availability depends on demand and audit requirements. Note that for BYOK/HSM we do envelope encryption: data keys are generated locally under customer CMK.

maria: Audit logs: customers asked about streaming to SIEMs and PII controls. What's possible today?

eli: Audit logs export options: JSON Lines (ndjson) and gzipped weekly bundles. Delivery targets: customer S3 buckets, SFTP, and streaming to Kafka or a webhook into SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog). Default retention: 90 days. Enterprise add-on allows custom retention up to 7 years. PII handling: Console offers pre-export redaction rules; you can whitelist/blacklist fields. Redaction happens server-side before logs leave Redwood. Example config snippet to send to S3 with redaction: ```json
{
  "destination": "s3://acme-redwood-audit/",
  "format": "ndjson",
  "retain_days": 3650,
  "redact": ["request.user.email","request.args.card_number"]
}```

elena: A couple of operational clarifications: (1) control plane network connectivity options; (2) checklist for Private/on-prem installs to satisfy auditors.

aya: Control plane connectivity: we offer PrivateLink endpoints and a secure peering option. For fully air-gapped/on-prem we provide a packaged control-plane artifact that runs inside customer network (customer ops owns upgrades). We'll publish a topology diagram and recommended firewall rules.

darius: Any changes to SLA / incident credit policies tied to these features?

maria: Legal note: SLA credits are in the enterprise SLA. Feature-specific credits (e.g., Private deployments misconfig due to customer network changes) are handled case-by-case. Security incidents follow the incident response timeline in our IR playbook and we issue a postmortem. For contract specific items, please cc enterprise-sales.

sanjay: Are there docs / runbooks for onboarding BYOK customers?

eli: Yes, we have a BYOK onboarding runbook (internal draft) with steps: create CMK, grant decrypt/encrypt to Redwood role, set alias, test rotation. I'll publish a public-facing trimmed guide and a more detailed internal guide for SEs.

zoe: Action items: Aya to publish SOC2/ISO dates + scope matrix; Eli to publish BYOK + audit-log export guides and example configs; EngInfra to add VPC/control-plane topology and Private install checklist; Legal will add notes on SLA/incident clauses for enterprise contracts. Please reply here if you want to be added to any follow-up doc or pilot.

matt: I want to be on the HSM pilot list.

eli: Added you, @matt.

elena: Thanks all. We'll update this thread with links once docs are live. If anything is urgent tag me. :spiral_note_pad:
